title: GPT-5 scoring links feedback monitoring reports with waking hippocampal ripple rates
summary: In a nine-participant intracranial EEG neurofeedback study, GPT-5 scored participants’ free-text reports on ten cognitive dimensions. Higher GPT-5-scored feedback monitoring was associated with lower hippocampal ripple rate (β=−2.71 events/min per SD, 95% CI −4.21 to −1.21; FDR q=.0108) across up to 27 participant-condition observations after adjustment for condition. This is an exploratory association in a small epilepsy-monitoring sample; the AI-derived ratings were not validated against human ratings or independently replicated, and do not establish causality.
ai_technology: GPT-5 large language model used to score free-text participant reports on ten cognitive dimensions
organization: The University of Osaka; The University of Tokyo; Juntendo University

evidence.tested: In nine participants undergoing intracranial EEG monitoring, GPT-5 scored reports from neurofeedback sessions; model-derived feedback-monitoring scores were associated with hippocampal ripple rates after adjustment for cognitive condition.
evidence.unknown: Only nine participants; no independent replication or human-rating comparison validated the GPT-5 scores. Prompt/model dependence and causal direction remain unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5 converted short free-text reports into ten structured cognitive-dimension scores; the feedback-monitoring score was the only one of ten dimensions associated with ripple rate after FDR correction.

source_review.scope: Full 30-page Research Square v1 primary preprint, including Methods pp.18–19 and Results figure legend p.30, plus abstract and source metadata.
